newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss police end Greenpeace nuclear blockade.
newsitem.headline: Swiss police end Greenpeace nuclear blockade.

text.p: Police broke up a blockade by Greenpeace activists that stalled two trucks carrying nuclear waste from a Swiss power plant for reprocessing in France or Britain, police and the environmentalist group said on Tuesday.
About 20 activists had chained themselves together across a road in Val de Travers, in the western Swiss canton of Neuchatel, for three and a half hours before police pulled dragged them aside.
Greenpeace blocked the road to press its demands for an end to reprocessing of nuclear fuel, which it said was polluting the world's oceans.
It also called on the Swiss government to refuse to let any more nuclear waste leave the country.
"We want the trucks to return to (Swiss nuclear utility) Muehleberg and not leave Switzerland," Greenpeace coordinator Stegfan Fueglister said by telephone from the scene.

Nuclear power plant operator BKW FMB Energie AG of Berne confirmed the two trucks were each carrying a 35 tonne security container for used nuclear fuel rods headed for reprocessing at La Hague, France, or Sellafield, England.
